title: The Price of Being Connected
text:
Many people now carry smartphones everywhere they go. These devices record location data, search history and messages, which companies can use to show targeted advertisements. Most users accept the terms of service without reading them carefully.

Governments also use surveillance cameras and facial recognition in some cities. Supporters say these tools help police prevent crime. Critics argue that constant monitoring reduces personal freedom, and they ask for clearer laws to protect citizens' privacy.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do smartphones record?
options: Location data, search history and messages

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do supporters say surveillance tools help police do?
Why do most users probably accept the terms of service without reading them?
options: The text is long or confusing, so they skip it
The law requires them to read it aloud
Companies pay them to skip it

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of constant monitoring?
options: The author is concerned about its effect on freedom
The author fully supports it without reservations
The author is indifferent to it

vocabulary.definition: the close watching of people, often by authorities
aimed at a specific group of people
people who express strong disapproval of something

paragraph_translations: Muitas pessoas hoje levam smartphones para todos os lugares. Esses aparelhos registram dados de localização, histórico de busca e mensagens, que as empresas podem usar para mostrar anúncios direcionados. A maioria dos usuários aceita os termos de serviço sem lê-los com atenção.

Os governos também usam câmeras de vigilância e reconhecimento facial em algumas cidades. Os defensores dizem que essas ferramentas ajudam a polícia a prevenir crimes. Os críticos argumentam que o monitoramento constante reduz a liberdade pessoal e pedem leis mais claras para proteger a privacidade dos cidadãos.
